message.content: {"action":"done","summary":"Milestone 2 implemented in tinydb/journal.py on top of the milestone-1 BatchWriter. R04: doc_id bool values are explicitly rejected (isinstance bool check before the int check); the whole batch is structurally validated before any commit - non-list operations, non-dict operations, non-dict documents, unknown ops and missing keys all raise ValueError with no state change; empty dict documents are accepted. R05: added preview(operations) which validates, then simulates on a deep-copied snapshot of the default table read from storage (keys normalised str->int for JSON storage); it never writes, never mutates the table's _next_id counter (reads it, falls back to max(id)+1 exactly like Table._get_next_id), and clears no caches, so data, the next insertion ID, existing table handles and query caches are all unchanged - including when the previewed batch errors. R05b: preview and apply both return fresh, detached lists; mutating a previously returned list has no effect on later results or writer state (tested). R05 clarification: a successful apply advances the table's next-insertion-ID counter and persists it through the storage write, so subsequent inserts via apply or direct db.insert continue the sequence without reuse or rewind even across removes; a failed apply restores the counter so no IDs are consumed. R06: every call re-reads current storage - no stale initial snapshot; direct db.insert calls between apply/preview calls are seen by the wrapper. The conflicting older note ('preview may consume IDs and bool IDs are accepted') is recorded and resolved in HANDOFF.md and the module docstring as superseded by R04/R05. Added ~60 new tests to tests/test_journal.py (now 123, parametrized over memory and JSON file storage). Verified: tests/test_journal.py 123 passed; full suite tests/ + acceptance_public.py = 350 passed; upstream test files confirmed unmodified (git status shows only new untracked files).","completion_asserted":true}
